notes: Address the user as "Anda" (always capitalised), polite but direct, as in Google/Microsoft Indonesian UIs. Buttons and menu items are short imperative verbs ("Simpan", "Batal", "Unduh sampul"); failure toasts use the passive "X gagal disimpan — coba lagi". Sentence case for labels, headings and buttons. Straight double quotes "…" around option names, as the English does; keep the English's "…" or "...". Familiar loanwords stay as Indonesian users know them: email, font, editor, offline, browser, pop-up, glossy, staples. Option names on Lulu's and Google Fonts' English-only sites stay in English; printer-dialog settings are given in Indonesian with the English in parentheses ("tepi pendek" (short edge)). Decimal comma (0,4in). LAI conventions for scripture: Bible = Alkitab, chapter = pasal, Bible book = kitab, Old/New Testament = Perjanjian Lama/Baru. A print interior is "isi buku" ("isi" alone = content); a printed copy is "eksemplar".
